codes.name: Foundational Misconception
codes.student_help: A core math rule was mixed up, like adding the bottoms of two fractions.
codes.description: A flawed mental model of what a quantity or operation means, applied consistently.
codes.example: 1/2 + 1/3 = 2/5 (adds numerators and denominators).

tell_apart.how: A one-off number slip with the right idea
A rule stretched beyond where it holds

codes.remediation: Concrete visual or area model of the idea, then the same item again.

codes.name: Sign / Direction Meaning
codes.student_help: A plus or minus sign, or a direction on a graph, was understood the wrong way.
codes.description: Misunderstands what a sign, direction or shift means, rather than slipping while calculating.
codes.example: Says y = (x - 3)^2 moves the parabola 3 left; reads a negative slope as rising.

tell_apart.how: Losing a sign while rearranging
A slip adding negatives

codes.remediation: Reference-frame sketch: plot two points and check the direction.

codes.name: Overgeneralised Rule
codes.plain_name: Rule used where it does not work
codes.student_help: A rule was used where it does not work, like squaring each term of (a + b) separately.
codes.description: Treats an operation as if it splits over a sum when it does not (false linearity), or cancels terms instead of factors.

tell_apart.how: Misusing a power law such as x^2 * x^3 = x^6

codes.remediation: Counterexample check: test the rule with small numbers before using it.

codes.name: Exponent Law Misuse
codes.student_help: A power rule was mixed up, like adding exponents when they should multiply.
codes.description: Misapplies the laws of exponents or what an exponent applies to.

tell_apart.how: A rule split over a sum, like (a + b)^2 = a^2 + b^2,

codes.remediation: Expand the power as repeated multiplication, then compare with the law.

codes.name: Like Terms Confusion
codes.student_help: Terms that are not alike were added together, like x^2 and x.
codes.description: Combines or cancels terms that have different variables or powers.

tell_apart.how: Dropping a term while collecting is PRC_STEP_OMITTED or PRC_SIGN_OR_FACTOR_DROPPED

codes.remediation: Colour-code terms by variable and power before collecting.

codes.name: Equation Balance
codes.student_help: Something was done to one side of the equation but not the other.
codes.description: Does not keep an equation balanced: operates on one side only, or treats = as 'the answer comes next'.
codes.example: 3x + 4 = 10 -> 3x = 10 (subtracts 4 on the left only); 2x + 3 = 11 = 8 = 4.

tell_apart.how: Using the wrong inverse operation on both sides (2x = 8 -> x = 6)
Run-on equals chains in otherwise correct work

codes.remediation: Balance-scale model: write the operation on both sides of every line.

codes.name: Domain / Restriction Blindness
codes.student_help: The answer uses a value that is not allowed here, like dividing by zero or a negative length.
codes.description: Ignores where an expression or situation is defined: divides by something that may be zero, roots a negative, keeps an impossible length or angle.
codes.example: Divides both sides of x^2 = 3x by x and loses x = 0; keeps a side length of -4 cm.

tell_apart.how: Not noticing an absurd final answer the student could have checked
Leaving out the negative root of x^2 = 9

codes.remediation: 'What values are allowed?' check before and after solving.

codes.name: Graph Feature Meaning
codes.student_help: A part of the graph was read as something else, like the y-intercept as a zero.
codes.description: Misunderstands what a graph feature means: intercepts vs zeros, slope vs intercept, vertex vs root, axis of symmetry.
codes.example: Gives the y-intercept as a zero of the parabola; reads the slope of y = 2x + 5 as 5.

tell_apart.how: Reading a value off the graph inaccurately with the right idea is FAC_ARITHMETIC_SLIP or COM_ILLEGIBLE_WORK
Picking the wrong equation for a graph in a setup

codes.remediation: Label each feature on a sketch and say what it means in words.

codes.name: Formula / Law Misselection
codes.student_help: The formula or rule used here does not fit this type of question.
codes.description: Applies a formula, theorem or law whose conditions the problem does not meet.
codes.example: Uses the sine law with three sides and no angle (needs the cosine law); uses SOH CAH TOA in a non-right triangle.

tell_apart.how: Right formula, wrong values in its slots
A misremembered version of the right formula

codes.remediation: Condition table: for each formula, list when it applies, then match the question.

codes.name: Word Problem Setup
codes.student_help: The words of the question were turned into the wrong equation.
codes.description: Translates a word problem, table or graph into an equation or model that does not match it.
codes.example: '5 less than twice a number is 11' written as 5 - 2x = 11; perimeter used where area is described.

tell_apart.how: A correct model with one given value misread
A mislabelled diagram

codes.remediation: Dimensional analysis table: name each quantity, its unit and how they relate before writing the equation.

codes.name: Diagram Misread
codes.student_help: The diagram was labelled the wrong way, like calling the wrong side the hypotenuse.
codes.description: Misidentifies parts of a diagram: opposite vs adjacent, hypotenuse, matching angles or sides in similar triangles.
codes.example: Uses the side next to the angle as 'opposite'; matches the wrong sides in a similar-triangle ratio.

tell_apart.how: Choosing trig when the triangle is not right-angled

codes.remediation: Mark the angle, then label opp, adj, hyp (or matching sides) on the diagram first.

codes.name: Wrong Substitution
codes.plain_name: Values put in the wrong places
codes.student_help: The right formula was used, but values went into the wrong spots.
codes.description: Puts known values into the wrong variables of a correct formula.
codes.example: Midpoint with ((x1 + y1)/2, (x2 + y2)/2); b and c swapped in the quadratic formula.

tell_apart.how: Using a formula that does not apply
Copying a value wrong

codes.remediation: Write 'a = , b = , c = ' (or x1, y1 ...) before substituting.

codes.name: No Viable Plan
codes.student_help: The first move here could not lead to the answer. Plan the method before writing.
codes.description: Starts with a move that cannot reach the answer, or moves symbols around with no method.
codes.example: Tries to solve x^2 + 5x + 6 = 0 by moving terms until x is alone; square-roots one term of a sum.

tell_apart.how: A valid method that is just long or not the one asked for

codes.remediation: Plan-first prompt: name the method in words before writing any maths.

codes.name: Unsuitable Method
codes.student_help: This method works, but it is not the one asked for, or it makes the question much longer.
codes.description: Uses a valid path that is not the one the question asked for, or one that makes the work much longer and error-prone.
codes.example: Question says 'solve by elimination' and the student graphs; completes the square on an easily factorable quadratic and then slips.

tell_apart.how: A method that cannot work at all

codes.remediation: Method comparison: solve the same item two ways side by side.

codes.name: Missing Case
codes.student_help: One possible answer or case was left out, like the negative square root.
codes.description: Does not consider every case the problem allows: the +/- root, both factors, a second triangle.
codes.example: x^2 = 49 -> x = 7 only; sets only one factor of (x - 2)(x + 5) = 0 to zero.

tell_apart.how: Dismissing a valid answer because of a wrong restriction
Skipping a whole sub-question

codes.remediation: 'How many answers could there be?' check before finishing.

codes.name: Ignored Condition
codes.student_help: A condition the question gave was not used, like 'x is positive' or a point on the line.
codes.description: Leaves a stated condition or given piece of information out of the model, so the answer does not meet it.
codes.example: Finds the line through (2, 3) with slope 4 but never uses the point; keeps a negative width when the question says it is positive.

tell_apart.how: Misreading the value of a given

codes.remediation: Underline every given and tick it off when it is used.

codes.name: Step Omission
codes.student_help: A needed step in the method was skipped.
codes.description: Skips a required step of the procedure, so the result does not follow.
codes.example: Completing the square without adding and subtracting (b/2)^2; finds x in a system but never finds y.

tell_apart.how: Stopping before the requested final form

codes.remediation: Faded worked example (about 80% done), then the full procedure.

codes.name: Order of Operations
codes.student_help: The steps were done in the wrong order.
codes.description: Applies valid rules in an invalid order (BEDMAS, or method steps out of sequence).
codes.example: 2 + 3 * 4 = 20; takes the square root before isolating the squared term.

tell_apart.how: Doing the inverse operation wrongly

codes.remediation: Parsons problem: put the given steps in order.

codes.name: Sign or Factor Dropped
codes.plain_name: Sign or term lost while rearranging
codes.student_help: A sign or a number got lost when expanding or moving terms around.
codes.description: Drops a sign, factor or term while expanding, factoring out, or moving terms, even though the method is right.

tell_apart.how: A consistent belief about signs
Adding or subtracting negatives wrongly

codes.remediation: Sign-tracking checkpoints: highlight every sign before and after the step.

codes.name: Wrong Inverse Operation
codes.plain_name: Undid a step the wrong way
codes.student_help: A step was undone with the wrong operation, like subtracting instead of dividing.
codes.description: Uses the wrong inverse when isolating a variable.

tell_apart.how: Applying the operation to one side only

codes.remediation: Write the operation being undone, then its inverse, next to each line.

codes.name: Inequality Direction
codes.student_help: The inequality sign should have flipped when multiplying or dividing by a negative.
codes.description: Does not reverse the inequality when multiplying or dividing by a negative (or reverses it when it should not).

tell_apart.how: Other sign slips while rearranging

codes.remediation: Test a number from the answer in the original inequality.

codes.name: Factoring Error
codes.student_help: The expression was factored into pieces that do not multiply back to it.
codes.description: Factors incorrectly: wrong pair of numbers, common factor only partly removed, or a difference of squares as a perfect square.

tell_apart.how: Solving each correct factor with the wrong sign
Not factoring fully

codes.remediation: Expand the factors back out to check before moving on.

codes.name: Combining Equations
codes.student_help: When combining the two equations, they were added when they should have been subtracted, or the reverse.
codes.description: In a linear system, combines equations with the wrong operation or substitutes back into the equation it came from.
codes.example: 4y and -4y with the equations subtracted instead of added; substitutes y = 2x - 1 back into the equation it came from and gets 0 = 0.

tell_apart.how: Not multiplying every term when scaling an equation

codes.remediation: Write which variable will cancel and why before combining.

codes.name: Incomplete Simplification
codes.student_help: The work stopped a step or two before the answer was fully simplified.
codes.description: Stops before reaching the simplified or requested form.
codes.example: Leaves 6/8; leaves sqrt(50) instead of 5 sqrt(2); stops at 2x = 10.

tell_apart.how: Giving an answer in a different form than asked (decimal for exact)

codes.remediation: Completion checklist: fractions reduced, radicals simplified, variable alone.

codes.name: Arithmetic Slip
codes.student_help: The steps make sense, with a small calculation slip in the numbers.
codes.description: An isolated arithmetic error with a sound method.
codes.example: 7 * 8 = 54 in the middle of a correct solution; 52/13 = 3.

tell_apart.how: A slip with negative numbers
A wrong recalled fact used repeatedly

codes.remediation: 5-item rapid micro-drill on the same kind of calculation.

codes.name: Signed Number Slip
codes.student_help: A slip happened when adding, subtracting or multiplying negative numbers.
codes.description: Arithmetic slip with negatives in otherwise correct work.

tell_apart.how: Not understanding what a negative means
Losing a sign during expansion

codes.remediation: Number-line check for each signed step.

codes.name: Copy Error
codes.student_help: A number or sign changed when copying from one line to the next.
codes.description: Miscopies a digit, sign or term from one of the student's own lines to the next.
codes.example: Line 3 says 3x + 12; line 4 starts 3x + 21.

tell_apart.how: Misreading the printed question

codes.remediation: Given-data check habit: compare each new line with the one above.

codes.name: Math Fact Recall
codes.student_help: A basic fact was remembered wrong, like a times-table fact or a perfect square.
codes.description: Misremembers a basic fact: times tables, squares and roots, exact trig values.

tell_apart.how: A misremembered formula

codes.remediation: Short fact fluency drill, then the item again.

codes.name: Formula Recall
codes.student_help: The right formula was chosen but remembered with a piece missing or changed.
codes.description: Picks the right formula but recalls it wrongly.
codes.example: Quadratic formula without 2a in the denominator; distance formula without the square root.

tell_apart.how: Choosing a formula that does not apply

codes.remediation: Formula card rebuild: write the formula from memory, then compare.

codes.name: Unit Conversion
codes.student_help: A unit conversion was off, like centimetres to metres.
codes.description: Converts units wrongly or mixes units in one calculation.
codes.example: 150 cm = 15 m; adds 2 m and 30 cm as 32.

tell_apart.how: Leaving units off the answer

codes.remediation: Dimensional conversion bridge: write the conversion factor as a fraction.

codes.name: Rounding / Precision
codes.student_help: A number was rounded too early or to the wrong decimal place.
codes.description: Rounds too early, or breaks the precision the question asks for.
codes.example: Rounds sin 37 deg to 0.6 mid-question and ends up 2 cm off; gives 3 decimals when asked for 1.

tell_apart.how: Giving a decimal when an exact answer is asked for

codes.remediation: Precision rule: keep full values until the last line.

codes.name: Calculator Entry
codes.student_help: The calculator was set up or used wrong, like being in radians instead of degrees.
codes.description: Wrong calculator mode, missing brackets when keying, or misread display.
codes.example: sin 30 = -0.988 (radian mode); keys -3^2 and gets -9 when (-3)^2 = 9 was meant.

tell_apart.how: A hand-arithmetic slip

codes.remediation: Calculator check: key a known value (sin 30 = 0.5) first.

codes.name: Answered a Different Question
codes.student_help: The work solved for something slightly different from what the question asked.
codes.description: Gives a correct answer to a different target than the one asked.
codes.example: Asked for the vertex, gives the zeros; asked for 2x + 5, stops at x.

tell_apart.how: The right target in the wrong format
Skipping a whole sub-part

codes.remediation: Pre-submission prompt check: circle what is asked, then reread the final line.

codes.name: Wrong Answer Form
codes.student_help: The answer is right, but not in the form the question asked for.
codes.description: Gives the right quantity in a form other than the one requested.
codes.example: Asked for vertex form, gives standard form; asked for an exact answer, gives 1.414; gives x = 2, y = 3 when a point is asked for.

tell_apart.how: Stopping before simplifying

codes.remediation: Underline the requested form in the question and match it.

codes.name: Missing Units
codes.student_help: The final answer is missing its units.
codes.description: Omits units on a measurement answer.
codes.example: Area = 24 (no cm^2); time = 3.5.

tell_apart.how: A wrong unit conversion

codes.remediation: Unit slot: draw a box for the unit next to every final answer.

codes.name: Missing Conclusion
codes.student_help: The question needed a closing sentence that answers it in words.
codes.description: Omits the concluding statement a word problem or proof requires.
codes.example: Word problem ends at t = 4 with no 'The ball lands after 4 s.'

tell_apart.how: Missing reasoning for a claim

codes.remediation: Concluding statement frame: 'Therefore, ...' using the question's words.

codes.name: Notation Misuse
codes.student_help: The maths is written in a way that says something different, like a long chain of equals signs.
codes.description: Misuses notation so the written statement is false or ambiguous, even if the thinking is right.
codes.example: 2x + 3 = 11 - 3 = 8 / 2 = 4; writes x + 2 * 3 meaning (x + 2) * 3; equals sign between an equation and its solution.

tell_apart.how: Doing an operation to one side only (a real balance error)

codes.remediation: One-equation-per-line layout model.

codes.name: Illegible Work
codes.student_help: Part of the working is too hard to read or follow.
codes.description: Handwriting or layout makes a line impossible to read or follow.
codes.example: Overwritten digits that could be 1 or 7; steps scattered around the page with no order.

tell_apart.how: When the photo itself is blurry, it is an upload problem, not an error code

codes.remediation: Grid workspace; ask for a clearer retake if the page is hard to read.

codes.name: Unsupported Answer
codes.student_help: The answer is there, but the reason the question asked for is missing.
codes.description: Gives an answer, claim or 'show that' conclusion without the reasoning or working the question requires.
codes.example: 'Show the triangles are similar' answered 'they are similar'; correct root written with no work when work is required.

tell_apart.how: A wrong answer with no work, likely guessed,

codes.remediation: 'Because ...' justification frame after every claim.

codes.name: Missing Labels / Definitions
codes.student_help: A graph, diagram or variable is missing labels, so it is unclear what it shows.
codes.description: Leaves out axis labels, scales, diagram labels or the 'let x be ...' definition that the work needs.
codes.example: Graph with no axis labels or scale; uses x and y in a word problem without saying what they are.

tell_apart.how: Units missing on a final answer

codes.remediation: Label checklist: axes, scale, units, and 'let x = ...'.

codes.name: Blank / Time Attrition
codes.student_help: This part was left blank.
codes.description: Leaves a question or part with no attempt, from time pressure or a frustration block.
codes.example: Question 5 is empty; the last two parts have nothing written.

tell_apart.how: Starting and then stopping

codes.remediation: Prerequisite baseline probe on the skill, then a first-step warm-up.

codes.name: Skipped Part
codes.student_help: One part of the question was skipped while the others were answered.
codes.description: Answers some parts of a multi-part question and leaves another out, likely without noticing.
codes.example: Finds x in (a) and the vertex in (c) but never answers (b).

tell_apart.how: Answering a different target
Leaving the whole question empty

codes.remediation: Tick each part number as it is answered.

codes.name: Distractor Trap
codes.plain_name: Middle step taken as the answer
codes.student_help: A middle step was treated as the final answer.
codes.description: Takes an intermediate value or a tempting wrong option as the final answer.
codes.example: Finds the discriminant and gives it as the root; picks the multiple-choice option that matches a half-way value.

tell_apart.how: Answering a different target from the start

codes.remediation: 'Is this what was asked?' stop sign before the final line.

codes.name: Abandoned Work
codes.student_help: A good start was stopped or crossed out before reaching an answer.
codes.description: Starts a valid approach, then stops or crosses it out partway with no answer.
codes.example: Sets up the quadratic formula correctly, substitutes, then stops.

tell_apart.how: No attempt at all

codes.remediation: First-step confidence warm-up, then the same problem.

codes.name: Erased Correct Work
codes.student_help: Correct work was crossed out and replaced with something wrong.
codes.description: Strikes out or erases correct work and replaces it with an incorrect answer.
codes.example: x = 4 crossed out, replaced with x = -4 which does not satisfy the equation.

tell_apart.how: Crossing out work and giving no answer

codes.remediation: Check-before-changing habit: substitute both answers before crossing one out.

codes.name: Unchecked Answer
codes.student_help: A quick check would show this answer cannot be right, like a negative length.
codes.description: Gives an answer a quick check would show is impossible or absurd, and does not notice.
codes.example: A side length of -3 cm; a probability of 1.4; a root that does not satisfy the equation.

tell_apart.how: Not knowing the value is disallowed

codes.remediation: Substitute-back or estimate check before finishing.

codes.name: Misread Given
codes.student_help: A number or sign in the question was read wrong.
codes.description: Misreads a number, sign or symbol printed in the question.
codes.example: Question says y = 2x^2 - 12x; work starts from y = 2x^2 + 12x.

tell_apart.how: Miscopying between the student's own lines
Misunderstanding the words

codes.remediation: Given-data check: compare line 1 with the question.

codes.name: Unworked Guess
codes.student_help: An answer was written with no working, and it is not right.
codes.description: Writes a wrong final answer with no working shown, suggesting a guess.
codes.example: 'x = 5' alone under a two-step equation whose answer is 3.

tell_apart.how: A correct answer missing the required reasoning

codes.remediation: Show-one-step rule: write at least the first step before any answer.
